description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review), Pass 3 of the ignored-tests audit (#993)
-- one of the clusters in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv that had no recorded
cause.  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

REPRO (scratch/p44-sig-qual.pl):

    sub int_handler { print "handler\n" }
    $SIG{INT} = "int_handler";
    print "[$SIG{INT}]\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  [main::int_handler]
  PCL:          [int_handler]

perl's %SIG set-magic qualifies an UNQUALIFIED handler name with the package
in effect at the assignment, so the value you read back is not the value you
wrote.  PCL stores the string as given.

WHAT IS ALREADY CORRECT (same probe): a CODE ref round-trips (`ref $SIG{INT}`
is CODE in both), and an ALREADY-qualified name is stored verbatim by both
(`$SIG{TERM} = "Foo::bar"` -> Foo::bar).  So the only divergence is the
qualification step on a bare name.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/magic.t 137, 138, 141, 142 (4 blessed rows in
baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, clustered as "%SIG key is reported unqualified
where perl qualifies it").  magic.t is a PARTIAL file, so these sit above its
abort point.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ROWS: the stored string is what a later `defined
$SIG{INT}` comparison, a save/restore idiom (`local $SIG{INT}; ... $SIG{INT} =
$old`) or a dispatch-by-name reads back.  Code that compares the read-back
value against the name it installed will disagree with perl.

FIX SHAPE (untried): qualify at the STORE, in %SIG's set-magic path, using the
package in effect -- the same `*pcl-current-package*` the caller machinery
already carries (docs/caller-implementation.md).  Only a bare name is
qualified: a name containing `::` and a code ref pass through.  Check the
sibling magic hashes at the same time (%ENV has its own store magic, cluster
"magic.t %ENV store", 10 rows and also unexplained -- probe whether they share
a store path before writing two fixes; CLAUDE.md rule 11).

=== HALF DONE (s494g, 2026-09-25, Opus) -- the SIGNAL-key half ===
#2107's %SIG store seam (%p-sig-qualify in %p-sig-set) now qualifies a bare handler NAME with `main::` for every SIGNAL key (always main, probed 5.40.3, even under `package P`); IGNORE / DEFAULT / "" / a name with `::` or `'` are stored as given.  magic.t `Can assign to INT` / `Can delete from INT` left baselines/fail-baseline.tsv by edit; local.t's two unnamed `local $SIG{...}` rows ('foo' vs 'main::foo') pass too (sweep TOTAL 18686 -> 18690, commit "sweep baselines edited row by row").
OPEN: the `__WARN__` / `__DIE__` keys are plain hash slots, not signal slots, so `$SIG{__WARN__} = "h"` still reads back `h` (magic.t `Can assign to __WARN__` / `Can delete from __WARN__` stay blessed).  The fix is the same qualification at those two keys' store.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `$SIG{INT} = "handler"` stores the NAME verbatim -- perl QUALIFIES an unqualified handler name with the current package (`main::handler`), so reading `$SIG{INT}` back gives a different string (owns magic.t 137/138/141/142)
